questions.question: How much blood is in a typical adult's body?
questions.fact: Men and women carry about the same share of their body weight as blood, 7 to 8%.

questions.question: How many bones are in an adult human skeleton?
questions.fact: Babies are born with around 270; some of them fuse together on the way to adulthood.

questions.question: How tall was Robert Wadlow, the tallest person ever recorded?
questions.fact: He weighed 199 kg when he died, aged 22.

questions.question: How long does an African bush elephant's pregnancy last?
questions.fact: It's the longest pregnancy of any mammal.

questions.question: How tall is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.fact: It was the tallest human-made structure in the world for 41 years, until New York's Chrysler Building was finished.

questions.question: What is the population of New York City?
questions.fact: An estimated 800 languages are spoken there, making it the most linguistically diverse city in the world.

questions.question: How long does the International Space Station take to circle Earth once?
questions.fact: That's 15.5 laps a day, so its crew sees 16 sunrises and sunsets every day.

questions.question: How many people walked on the Moon during the Apollo program?
questions.fact: Six Apollo landings each set two astronauts down on the surface while a third waited in orbit.

questions.question: How hot must the oven be for a true Neapolitan pizza?
questions.fact: At that heat the pizza bakes in 60 to 90 seconds.

questions.question: How many passengers can an Airbus A380, the biggest airliner, carry?
questions.fact: In the evacuation test, everyone got out in 78 seconds with half the exits blocked.

questions.question: How much water does an Olympic swimming pool hold?
questions.fact: It's 50 m long, 25 m wide and at least 2 m deep: 2,500 cubic metres of water.

questions.question: How far is a marathon?
questions.fact: The distance was fixed in 1921, copied from the course of the 1908 London Olympics.

questions.question: How long did the longest professional tennis match last?
questions.fact: John Isner beat Nicolas Mahut 70-68 in the fifth set, after 11 hours 5 minutes spread over three days.

source.title: Isner–Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships

questions.question: How many keys does a modern piano have?
questions.fact: In Mozart's day pianos had five octaves; today's 88 keys span more than seven.

questions.question: How much beer do Czechs, the world's top beer drinkers, get through a year?
questions.fact: That's about 250 half-litre glasses for every Czech, children included, and no country drinks more.

source.title: List of countries by beer consumption per capita

questions.question: How long is the record for holding your breath?
questions.definition: official freediving record, breathing only air first
questions.fact: Breathe pure oxygen beforehand and the record is over 29 minutes.

questions.question: How much does an ostrich egg weigh?
questions.fact: That is over 20 times a chicken's egg, yet it's the smallest egg of any bird relative to the mother's size.

questions.question: How fast can a hummingbird's heart beat?
questions.definition: fastest measured, in a blue-throated hummingbird
questions.fact: At night, in a torpor, a hummingbird's heart can slow to around 50 beats a minute.

questions.question: How fast can a cheetah run?
questions.fact: Its acceleration is the real weapon: from 0 to 97 km/h in under 3 seconds.

questions.question: How many people live in Antarctica in winter?
questions.fact: In summer the number swells to about four times that.

questions.question: How many hot dogs did the record holder eat in 10 minutes?
questions.fact: In 2001 Takeru Kobayashi ate 50, nearly doubling the old record of 25.5.

questions.question: How fast does Earth spin at the equator?
questions.fact: It slows away from the equator: about 1,184 km/h at 45° latitude, and zero at the poles.

questions.question: How fast did Usain Bolt run at his top speed?
questions.definition: during his 100 m world record, 9.58 s
questions.fact: His average over the whole race, start included, was 37.58 km/h.

questions.question: How high is the men's high jump world record?
questions.fact: Javier Sotomayor set it in 1993, and nobody has beaten it since.

source.title: Men's high jump world record progression

questions.question: How much of the Moon's surface can we see from Earth?
questions.fact: It always turns the same face to us, but it wobbles as it orbits, so we see a little way round its edges.

questions.question: In what year did the Wright brothers first fly a plane?
questions.fact: That first flight, at Kitty Hawk in North Carolina, lasted 12 seconds and covered 37 metres.

questions.question: In what year was the first video uploaded to YouTube?
questions.fact: Called Me at the Zoo, it is 19 seconds of co-founder Jawed Karim in front of the elephants at San Diego Zoo.

questions.question: How much does a fingernail grow in a month?
questions.fact: Toenails grow about half as fast, about 1.6 mm a month, and a whole fingernail takes three to six months to regrow.

questions.question: How old was the oldest person whose age has been verified?
questions.fact: Jeanne Calment of France lived 122 years and 164 days, and said that at 13 she had met Vincent van Gogh in her uncle's shop.

questions.question: How long is a day on the Moon, from one sunrise to the next?
questions.fact: It matches the cycle of the Moon's phases, because the Moon turns once per orbit and always shows us the same face.

questions.question: How long did NASA's Perseverance rover take to fly from Earth to Mars?
questions.fact: It left in a launch window of under a month, when Earth and Mars were best placed for the trip, alongside missions from China and the UAE.

questions.question: How long is the longest single trip anyone has made in space?
questions.fact: Valeri Polyakov spent it on the Mir space station, to learn how a human body would cope with a long trip to Mars.

questions.question: How many eggs can a laying hen produce in a year?
questions.fact: The record is 371 eggs in 364 days.

questions.question: How much food can an elephant eat in a day?
questions.fact: Less than half of it gets digested, so its dung feeds other animals, from dung beetles to monkeys.

questions.question: How old are the oldest known remains of bread?
questions.fact: It was found at a Natufian site in Jordan's north-eastern desert, and is thousands of years older than farming.

questions.question: How much did one US penny, the 1-cent coin, cost to make?
questions.fact: Losing money on every coin is largely why the Mint stopped making pennies for circulation in November 2025.

questions.question: How fast did Concorde, the supersonic passenger jet, fly?
questions.fact: That's more than twice the speed of other airliners, so it crossed the Atlantic in just under 3.5 hours.

questions.question: How long is a football pitch?
questions.definition: FIFA's recommended size for top matches
questions.fact: The Laws of the Game allow anything from 91 to 119 m, so pitches really do vary.

questions.question: How far does a rider cycle in the Tour de France, the three-week race?
questions.fact: It's split into 21 stages over three weeks, with only two rest days.

questions.question: How long did the fastest Formula One pit stop take?
questions.fact: A crew of up to 20 mechanics changes all four tyres in that time.

questions.question: How much was the most expensive football transfer ever?
questions.fact: It more than doubled the previous record, Paul Pogba's move to Manchester United a year earlier.

source.title: List of most expensive association football transfers

questions.question: How many people have ever been born?
questions.fact: That makes the people alive today about 6.7% of everyone who has ever lived.

questions.question: How long ago did our species, Homo sapiens, first appear?
questions.fact: For all but the last 12,000 or so of those years, every human lived as a hunter-gatherer.

questions.question: How far away is the horizon when you look out to sea?
questions.definition: standing on the beach, eyes 1.7 m up
questions.fact: Climb a 100 m tower and it's 35.7 km away.

questions.question: How fast does a skydiver fall before the parachute opens?
questions.fact: Jumping from 38,887 m up, where the air is thin, Felix Baumgartner reached 380 m/s, about 1,368 km/h.

questions.question: How many oil paintings did Vincent van Gogh make?
questions.fact: With drawings and watercolours he made about 2,100 works, most of them in the last two years of his life.
questions.definition: in a career of just over ten years

questions.question: How much did the most expensive painting ever sold go for?
questions.fact: Decades earlier it had sold for just £45, when it was thought to be the work of a follower.

questions.question: How many people watched the first Moon landing live on TV?
questions.fact: That was roughly one in five of everyone alive at the time.

questions.question: How long did it take to build the Empire State Building?
questions.definition: first steel columns to opening day
questions.fact: At its fastest the frame rose by about four and a half floors a week.

questions.question: How deep is the deepest hole ever drilled?
questions.fact: It took 19 years to drill, and got only about a third of the way through the crust beneath it.

questions.question: How much did the first handheld mobile phone weigh?
questions.definition: Motorola DynaTAC, the version approved for sale
questions.fact: A full charge took about 10 hours and gave just 30 minutes of talking.

questions.question: How many heartbeats does a person have in a lifetime?
questions.fact: A resting adult heart beats 60 to 100 times a minute, so even a slow one tops 86,000 beats a day.

questions.question: How much blood does the heart pump in a day?
questions.fact: At rest it pushes out about 70 ml with each beat, some 70 times a minute.

questions.question: How many teeth does an adult have?
questions.definition: a full set, wisdom teeth included
questions.fact: Children have 20 baby teeth, and the wisdom teeth at the back usually come through between 17 and 25.

questions.question: How many times a minute does a person blink?
questions.fact: Reading or staring at one thing slows it to about 4 or 5 a minute.

questions.question: Spending a dollar a second, how long would a billion dollars last?
questions.fact: At the same rate a million dollars would be gone in under 12 days.

questions.question: How many matches were played at the 2026 World Cup?
questions.definition: 48 teams, in groups of four, then knockouts
questions.fact: Twelve groups of four played six matches each, and the knockout rounds from the last 32 added 32 more.

questions.question: How many spaces are there around a Monopoly board?
questions.fact: Twenty-eight of them are properties to buy: 22 streets, four railroads and two utilities.

questions.question: How many panels make up a classic black-and-white football?
questions.fact: Twelve are pentagons and twenty are hexagons, the pattern that made the ball a symbol of the game.

questions.question: How many smartphones were shipped worldwide in 2019?
questions.fact: Shipments first topped a billion a year in 2013, when smartphones passed half of all mobile phones sold.

questions.question: How many cars are there in the world?
questions.fact: Between them they burn over a trillion litres of petrol and diesel a year.

questions.question: How many calories are in a Big Mac?
questions.fact: Over half of them, 306, come from its fat.

questions.question: How much pasta does an Italian eat in a year?
questions.definition: per person, by weight as sold, 2015
questions.fact: That's the most of any country, ahead of Tunisia at 16 kg a person.

questions.question: How many people live in Vatican City, the smallest country?
questions.fact: They are clergy and other religious, the Swiss Guard and lay staff, and their families.

questions.question: How long ago did the last woolly mammoths die out?
questions.fact: Most had died out at the end of the Ice Age, but a few hung on until then on Wrangel Island, off Siberia.

questions.question: How far is it from the North Pole to the equator?
questions.fact: The metre was first defined as one ten-millionth of this distance, which is why it's so round.

questions.question: How many time zones does Russia span?
questions.fact: It is the largest country in the world, and it borders fourteen others.

questions.question: How many countries are there in Africa?
questions.fact: Most of them kept the borders drawn by colonial powers when they became independent.

questions.question: How many people does a group need for an even chance two share a birthday?
questions.fact: With 23 people there are 253 pairs, and each pair is a fresh chance of a match.

questions.question: How much sugar is in a can of Coca-Cola?
questions.fact: It gives the can all of its 140 calories, since there is no fat in it.

questions.question: How long is the ball in play during a football match?
questions.fact: Stoppage time doesn't make up for all the time lost to throw-ins, free kicks and goal kicks.

questions.question: How many sheep are there in New Zealand?
questions.fact: It once had 39 million, nearly 10 for every New Zealander, before forests took over farmland.

questions.question: How far does a Formula One car race in a Grand Prix?
questions.fact: Monaco, on narrow city streets, is the one exception, at 260 km.

questions.question: How many sheets of A4 paper would cover a square metre?
questions.fact: A0 is exactly one square metre, and each size down is half the one before, so A4 is a sixteenth.

questions.question: How many McDonald's are there in the United States?
questions.fact: Mainland China comes next with over 7,700, then Japan with over 3,000.

source.title: List of countries with McDonald's restaurants

questions.question: How many people speak English?
questions.definition: as a first or second language, 2026
questions.fact: Only about 450 million of them are native speakers.

source.title: List of languages by total number of speakers

questions.question: What share of Earth's water is fresh water?
questions.fact: About 69% of that is frozen as ice and snow, and only 0.3% is liquid water at the surface.

questions.question: What share of Earth's land is covered by forest?
questions.fact: More than half of all forest is in just five countries: Russia, Brazil, Canada, the US and China.

questions.question: What share of the Netherlands lies below sea level?
questions.fact: About 21% of the Dutch live below sea level too, on land kept dry by dykes, canals and pumping stations.

questions.question: What share of the world's people live south of the equator?
questions.fact: It holds only 32.7% of Earth's land, since 80.9% of its surface is water.

questions.question: What share of Earth's mammals, by weight, are wild, not people or farm animals?
questions.fact: On land it's under 2%: nearly all the rest is people and farm animals.

questions.question: What share of the world's people use the internet?
questions.fact: That's up from 60% in 2020, but still leaves about 2.2 billion people offline.

questions.question: What share of all known animal species are beetles?
questions.fact: With hundreds of thousands of described species, beetles are the largest order of all, and almost 40% of known arthropods.

questions.question: On Mars, what share of your Earth weight would you feel?
questions.fact: Mars is about half Earth's width but has only 11% of its mass, so it pulls far less.

questions.question: What share of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil?
questions.fact: Peru has 13% and Colombia 10%, and six more countries and territories share the rest.

questions.question: What share of Greenland is covered by ice?
questions.fact: If it all melted, the oceans would rise by about 7.4 m.

questions.question: What share of an avocado's flesh is fat?
questions.fact: Most of the rest is water, about 73%.

questions.question: What share of men are red-green colour blind?
questions.fact: In women it's only about 0.5%, because the genes for it sit on the X chromosome.

questions.question: What share of the world's earthquakes hit the Ring of Fire, around the Pacific's edge?
questions.fact: The belt runs about 40,000 km around the Pacific, and holds about two thirds of the world's volcanoes too.

questions.question: What share of people are left-handed?
questions.fact: If both parents are left-handed, their child has a 26% chance of being left-handed too.

questions.question: What share of an adult's body weight is water?
questions.fact: Muscle is about 75% water and fat only about 10%, so the share varies from person to person.

questions.question: How much of the London Underground actually runs underground?
questions.fact: Most of the track out in the open is north of the River Thames, on the lines' long outer branches.

questions.question: How much of Earth's surface does the Pacific Ocean cover?
questions.fact: That's more than all of Earth's land put together.

questions.question: How much of the world's coffee does Brazil grow?
questions.fact: Vietnam comes second, and in the 1910s Brazil exported about 70% of all the world's coffee.

questions.question: How much of the world's maple syrup comes from Quebec?
questions.fact: Almost all the rest comes from the rest of Canada and from the United States.

questions.question: What share of penalty kicks are scored?
questions.fact: In World Cup penalty shootouts only 69.4% go in.

questions.question: What share of the world's people live where cars drive on the left?
questions.fact: The 75 countries that drive on the left cover only about a sixth of the world's land.

questions.question: What share of Icelanders live in and around Reykjavík?
questions.fact: The city itself has about 140,000 people, and six towns around it make up the rest.

questions.question: How much of Switzerland do the Alps cover?
questions.fact: Yet most of its 9 million people live on the flatter plateau to the north, around Zurich, Geneva and Basel.

questions.question: What share of Canadians live within 150 km of the US border?
questions.fact: That leaves about a fifth of the people for the rest of the world's second-largest country.

questions.question: How much of an iceberg is under the water?
questions.fact: Ice is only a little lighter than seawater: about 920 kg a cubic metre against 1,025.

questions.question: When did the first iPhone go on sale?
questions.fact: It launched without an App Store, which only opened a year later.

questions.question: When was the first email sent from one computer to another?
questions.fact: Ray Tomlinson sent it over ARPANET, and picked the @ sign to separate the user's name from the computer's.

questions.question: When was the first text message sent to a mobile phone?
questions.fact: It read 'Merry Christmas', and was typed on a personal computer and sent to a colleague's phone.

questions.question: When were the first bitcoins created?
questions.fact: The first notable purchase of goods with them came the next year: two pizzas for ten thousand bitcoins.

questions.question: When did the Titanic sink?
questions.fact: It went down on its maiden voyage, less than three hours after hitting an iceberg.

questions.question: When was the first satellite, Sputnik 1, launched?
questions.fact: It circled Earth every 96 minutes, beeping, until its batteries died three weeks later.

questions.question: When were the first modern Olympic Games held?
questions.fact: They took place in Athens, with 241 athletes from 14 nations, all of them men.

questions.question: When was the first Harry Potter book published?
questions.fact: Most publishers thought it too long, until the eight-year-old daughter of Bloomsbury's boss said it was 'so much better than anything else'.

source.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

questions.question: When was the modern Lego brick designed?
questions.fact: Bricks made that year still click together with the ones sold today.

questions.question: When did Alexander Fleming discover penicillin?
questions.fact: He spotted a mould killing the bacteria on a dish he had left out while away on holiday.

questions.question: When did the world's first underground railway open, in London?
questions.fact: Steam engines pulled its trains, filling stations and carriages with smoke, until the line was electrified in 1905.

questions.question: When was Mount Everest first climbed to the top?
questions.fact: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the top on 29 May, and the news broke in London on the morning of Queen Elizabeth II's coronation.

questions.question: When was Coca-Cola invented?
questions.fact: John Pemberton first sold it at an Atlanta pharmacy for five cents a glass, as an alcohol-free take on his coca wine tonic.

questions.question: When was the first human heart transplant?
questions.fact: Christiaan Barnard did it in Cape Town, and his patient lived for 18 days.

questions.question: When was Pluto demoted from planet to dwarf planet?
questions.fact: The find of Eris, an icy world beyond Neptune more massive than Pluto, forced astronomers to define a planet.

questions.question: When did euro coins and notes go into circulation?
questions.fact: The euro itself began in 1999, but at first only on screens and in bank accounts.

questions.question: When were the first traffic lights put up?
questions.fact: A police officer raised and lowered their semaphore arms by day and, at night, worked a lever for red and green lights.

questions.question: When was the first football World Cup played?
questions.fact: Uruguay hosted it to mark 100 years of its independence, and won it.

questions.question: When did the world's population reach 4 billion?
questions.fact: It took only 48 years more to double again, to 8 billion in November 2022.

questions.question: When did people first fly, in a hot-air balloon?
questions.fact: Étienne Montgolfier, of a family of French paper makers, went up first, tethered, from a Paris workshop yard.

questions.question: When did Elizabeth II become queen?
questions.fact: She was 25, and reigned for 70 years and 214 days, the longest of any British monarch.

questions.question: When did the World Wide Web open to everyone?
questions.fact: Tim Berners-Lee had it running at CERN by the end of 1990, then released it to the whole internet.

questions.question: When did anyone last walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: It was Apollo 17, and no one flew beyond low Earth orbit again until a Moon flyby in April 2026.

questions.question: When was the first selfie taken?
questions.fact: Robert Cornelius, an American photography pioneer, took it, and wrote on the back that it was 'the first light picture ever taken'.
